# Education in Poland
The Polish education system transitioned significantly through major reforms. Prior to 2017, the structure consisted of 6 years of primary school, followed by a mandatory 3-year junior high school ($\text{gimnazjum}$), and then upper secondary education. The 2017 "Law on School Education" abolished the $\text{gimnazjum}$ and extended primary school to eight years, while also extending the duration of upper secondary education.
Upper secondary education encompasses general secondary schools ($\text{liceum}$), which allow students to pass the "Matura" exam for higher education, and vocational/technical schools ($\text{technikum}$ or $\text{zasadnicza szkoła zawodowa}$). The system adheres to the Bologna scheme in higher education, featuring a three-year bachelor's degree followed by a two-year master's degree, though some fields, like medicine and pharmacy, have longer, unique-cycle programs. University grading uses a numerical system from 2.0 (failing) to 5.0 (highest grade), assessed every semester.
